rationale: This is a 190-byte, 4-function C++ program (a boolean-logic NP benchmark with tiny True/False class methods), so size overhead is nearly free while correctness of the small polymorphic-looking methods matters most. SUB gets the highest weights across security and diversity because instruction substitution is cheap, safe, and effective on such small functions where every instruction carries signal. FLA and BCF are strongly weighted (security 0.75/0.65) since flattening and bogus control flow give the largest semantic-hiding payoff per byte on code this small, and their modest absolute size/runtime cost is acceptable at 190 text bytes; BCF's runtime weight is kept moderate because tiny functions may run in tight loops. IBR is moderately weighted to diversify basic-block layout cheaply. SPLIT is weighted mainly for diversity (it synergizes with FLA by creating more blocks) but kept low on security since splitting alone reveals little. ICALL and especially IGV carry elevated CorrectnessRisk weights: indirect calls through C++ member functions (True::and_m, False::and_m with class-pointer parameters) and indirect global access risk ABI/vtable-related breakage and complicate the already-recursive-looking dispatch in main, so they remain eligible for feature-favored functions but are discouraged unless feature scores strongly favor them. No pass is fully disabled so the feature-driven selector retains freedom on individual functions.
